# Objective

Const values should be more ergonomic to insert, since this is too verbose
``` rust
#[derive(Component)]
#[require(
    LockedAxes(||LockedAxes::ROTATION_LOCKED),
)]
pub struct CharacterController;
```
instead, users can now abbreviate that nonsense like this
``` rust
#[derive(Component)]
#[require(
    LockedAxes = ROTATION_LOCKED),
)]
pub struct CharacterController;
```
it also works for enum labels.
I chose to omit the type, since were trying to reduce typing here. The alternative would have been this:
```rust
#[require(
    LockedAxes = LockedAxes::ROTATION_LOCKED),
)]
```
This of course has its disadvantages, since the const has to be associated, but the old closure method is still possible, so I dont think its a problem.
- Fixes #16720

## Testing

I added one new test in the docs, which also explain the new change. I also saw that the docs for the required components on line 165 was missing an assertion, so I added it back in

issue_context.title: Required components should accept constant and enum values of the appropriate type
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

When defining a component, we can specify that certain other components are required. Ordinarily, this inserts them with their default value.

```rust
#[derive(Component)]
#[require(
    LockedAxes(||LockedAxes::ROTATION_LOCKED),
)]
pub struct CharacterController;
```

If we want to override that, we can pass any function which takes no argument, and returns the appropriate component type.

```rust
#[derive(Component)]
#[require(
    LockedAxes(||LockedAxes::ROTATION_LOCKED),
)]
pub struct CharacterController;
```

However, this is verbose / frustrating when working with constants.

## What solution would you like?

Users should be able to pass in a constant, like so:

```rust
#[derive(Component)]
#[require(
  LockedAxes::ROTATION_LOCKED,
)]
pub struct CharacterController;
```

I suspect that we'll need to generate a closure that constructs the constant, but I haven't looked closely at the code here. We will need to require `Clone` unless we're storing a closure.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

If, for macro reasons, we absolutely need to pass in the type before the constructor, we could do:

```rust
#[derive(Component)]
#[require(
    LockedAxes(LockedAxes::ROTATION_LOCKED),
)]
pub struct CharacterController;
```

## Additional context

We might also want to provide helpers for doing this for dynamically registered components.
comments:
IMO a syntax using `=` instead of the nested parentheses would look cleaner in general:

```rust
#[derive(Component)]
#[require(
    LockedAxes = LockedAxes::ROTATION_LOCKED,
)]
pub struct CharacterController;
```

This also matches the upcoming default field values feature in Rust.

What was the motivation for taking a function-like expression instead of one that simply evaluates to the component's type? Just to avoid having to type `()` if it *is* a function?

> What was the motivation for taking a function-like expression instead of one that simply evaluates to the component's type? Just to avoid having to type () if it is a function?

You would need a Clone bound otherwise as you copy the value repeatedly, which isn't necessarily desirable. I also expect this to be expanded with access to more data as part of the `Construct` work, which definitely needs to be functionlike.

review_comments: We could parse out an expression instead and support more ways to set the value.
yes, but you would somehow need to extract the type from the expression, so it will be messy
